status: Production-ready narration/storyboard draft; no final audio alignment or rendered-film review attested.
voice_timing_note: 24 independent 7.5-second edit slots. Target 6.5 seconds of speech plus 1 second of visual breathing room per slot. The 180-second picture timeline is exact; generated voice duration is not yet verified. Align natural speech in the final edit and trim pauses, never imply provider timing from edited waits.

creative_direction.voice: One consistent English voice: curious, clear, confident, conversational; about 138 words/minute during voiced portions. No trailer announcer. Stress select, lock, reveal, and measure. Pronounce Twinforge as twin-forge and SAM 3.1 as Sam three point one.
creative_direction.editing: Lead with the product and a visible question. Alternate tight details and wide interface views. Keep the lock/reveal sequence continuous within one run. Use brief silence before Reveal and after the actual error. One visual claim at a time; never speed-scroll evidence.
creative_direction.sound: Low instrumental pulse under speech; drop the bed for the locked-target reveal. Sparse UI clicks. Editorial sound effects are not sensor measurements.
creative_direction.graphics: English throughout. Amber = prediction, cyan = later tracked observation. Use actual UI captures for capabilities. Generated shots may illustrate future use or transitions only, always visibly labelled.

verified_trial.source_description: Uploaded recording of actual hand movement; not synthetic photo motion and not a live phone-camera test.
verified_trial.reference: Later visual tracker positions, not independent annotations. Individual trial, not a general performance guarantee.
verified_trial.prior_failures: Previous trials and their failures remain in the linked report; do not overwrite them or claim a controlled before/after improvement.

segments.title: The question
segments.en: A camera shows you what just happened. Twinforge asks: where will this object be next?
segments.shot: Actual Twinforge randomized scene, cropped tightly around one moving object. Freeze the edit just before a visible event; this editorial freeze is not a locked prediction. Reveal the product name in the last second.

segments.title: What the product does
segments.en: Select an object. Predict its position. Test the result. A forecast becomes a measurable claim.
segments.shot: Three quick actual-interface cuts: select an object, show its issued forecast, show a later measured result. Do not fabricate a result or splice one run's target into another run.

segments.title: Make Meta visible
segments.en: Meta's SAM three point one segments the object. Twinforge tracks it and estimates its next position.
segments.shot: Open the actual submitted-frame/mask preview. Highlight the real SAM 3.1 label and mask; then cut back to the forecast.
segments.required_label: Real SAM result · separate local forecast

segments.title: The honest boundary
segments.en: The input is pixels. No simulator coordinates, hidden velocity feed, or prerecorded future trajectory.
segments.shot: Minimal editorial diagram: renderer → captured image → observer. The image is the only payload crossing the boundary apart from prompts and capture IDs/timestamps. No scrolling fake terminal.

segments.title: A fresh scene
segments.en: Start a new trial: randomized launches, collisions, or pendulums. Different starting conditions. A fresh observation.
segments.shot: Record real New scene actions across launch/rebound, collisions, and pendulum. Short cuts may compress resets; retain scene labels and never imply unknown physical laws were discovered.

segments.title: Show what is withheld
segments.en: The renderer knows its world. Our observer never receives its positions, velocities, masses, or forces.
segments.shot: Hold the pixel preview next to the rendered scene. A restrained graphic lists the withheld state: position, velocity, mass, force. Do not show invented source-code output.

segments.title: Three distinct jobs
segments.en: Here is the division: SAM finds the object. Local tracking follows it. Twinforge forecasts its motion.
segments.shot: Animate three plain labels using the actual mask, observed trail, and forecast as examples. Each visual is labelled by its actual producing component.

segments.title: Choose the challenge
segments.en: Choose half a second, three quarters, or one second ahead. Shading shows conditional uncertainty.
segments.shot: Actual horizon control: 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 seconds. Show the uncertainty region without depicting it as a guaranteed confidence bound.

segments.title: Freeze the claim
segments.en: Lock a target before the future arrives. Its position and timestamp are now fixed.
segments.shot: Continuous capture of Lock prediction in a synthetic run. Hold the target and its source/target timestamps. Keep this exact run for the next shot.

segments.title: Let time answer
segments.en: Reveal. The scene advances. Amber is the prediction. Cyan is the later observation. Measure the gap.
segments.shot: Continue the previous capture through Reveal and the measured outcome. Amber target stays fixed. Hold the actual error number long enough to read; never substitute a lower error.
segments.required_label: Error measured against later visual tracking

segments.title: Keep the record honest
segments.en: Keep the misses. Keep unscorable attempts. Each result stays tied to its source and horizon.
segments.shot: Open that run's actual scored/unscorable counts or export. Show one real unscorable record alongside measured results, with no invented percentages.
segments.required_label: Individual run · not a universal accuracy claim

segments.title: Your images
segments.en: Now use camera mode, or open a local video. Tap an object. Box a bottle.
segments.shot: Show actual camera-mode controls and native point/box selection on the bottle fixture. If using the existing fixture, its photo-motion label must remain visible. A phone mockup is layout illustration only.
on_screen: TAP AN OBJECT · DRAW A BOX

segments.title: Real hand movement
segments.en: Choose Hands. SAM finds visible hands. This example uses a recording of real human movement.
segments.shot: Use the retained real-hand run, preferably v16, and its corresponding original hand clip. Show Hands selection and actual SAM mask. Do not use the two-hand synthetic photo-motion clip here.
segments.required_label: Uploaded real hand video · not a live phone test

segments.title: An uncertain human future
segments.en: The fingers change shape. The hand changes direction. We forecast overall motion, not intention.
segments.shot: Continue that real-hand run through a direction or shape change. Keep both the observed position and predicted point visible; retain visible disagreement.

segments.title: An auditable number
segments.en: In this recorded trial, one-second forecasts averaged thirty-four pixels of error across fifty-seven scored targets.
segments.shot: Show a clean result card derived from real-hand-1-v16.json, paired with that exact run. This may be an editorial data card; label it Recorded trial, never Live measurement.

segments.title: The denominator matters
segments.en: Eight more were unscorable. These comparisons use later visual tracking, not independent ground truth.
segments.shot: Continue the same card: add 8 unscorable outcomes, and identify the comparison method. Do not turn this into a success percentage or accuracy guarantee.

segments.title: Two different clocks
segments.en: Local tracking ran around twenty-five frames per second. SAM inference ran separately, with its latency measured.
segments.shot: Use the same v16 measurements. Show local observed cadence separately from the two retained SAM provider response times, and keep client round-trip timing in smaller readable text.

segments.title: Stay responsive while waiting
segments.en: During that wait, captured frames keep arriving. SAM's confirmed mask anchors tracking through those observations.
segments.shot: Actual refresh capture after an established SAM anchor: local movement continues while a later SAM request is pending. Initial synthetic/video acquisition may pause; do not use that initial wait as the example.
segments.required_label: Any compressed wait must be labelled

segments.title: Open the proof
segments.en: Open the evidence: submitted image, segmentation mask, request receipts, prediction timestamps, and measured outcomes.
segments.shot: Actual evidence dialog: submitted frame and its mask, then real receipt/timestamp fields. Mask must correspond to the displayed frame. Hide credentials; do not invent a diagnostic dashboard.

segments.title: Make it inspectable
segments.en: Export the record. Anyone reviewing it can ask: was this claim recorded before its outcome?
segments.shot: Click the real export action. Show a readable excerpt with the same run ID and issue/target/observation times; timestamps must come from that file.

segments.title: What exists today
segments.en: Today, Twinforge forecasts two-dimensional image positions. Physical reconstruction and robot control are future work.
segments.shot: Return to a clear wide product view. Use two simple labels: built today, future work. No robot actuation footage presented as implemented functionality.
segments.required_label: No full 3D reconstruction or robot control

segments.title: Where it could matter
segments.en: The potential is practical: help robotics teams test anticipation before trusting predictions with real actions.
segments.shot: Optional short generated robotics concept shot, visually distinct from the app capture, or a clean editorial diagram of perception → forecast → test. No fake SAM overlays or claims of deployed hardware.

segments.title: The next experiment
segments.en: Next: independent annotations, harder motion, and physical device trials. Keep testing the limits.
segments.shot: Three concise roadmap cards over actual hand/simulation stills: independent annotations, harder motion, device trials. These are next steps, not completed validations.

segments.title: End on the product
segments.en: Twinforge. See motion. Freeze a forecast. Measure what happens next. Then improve the next prediction.
segments.shot: Return to the real UI and logo. Resolve to the public source/evidence URL; keep it readable through the final second. Do not identify the owner-private backend as public jury access.

review_requirements: Final picture duration must be exactly 180 seconds; at 30 fps this is 5400 frames. Verify the exported media, not just the edit grid.
Review the complete film with audio and again muted. Subtitles must match actual speech and fit mobile-readable safe margins.
Do not claim that SAM predicts motion: SAM segments; local tracking and the separate Twinforge predictor handle motion.
Do not attribute 25 Hz local capture/tracking to the SAM provider. Keep inference and client round-trip times distinct.
Do not fake a mask, a receipt, a successful lock outcome, a mobile camera test, or a physical-control demonstration.
Every lock/reveal pair must use the same real run and unchanged issued target. Any displayed error comes from its export.
The 34.10 px / 57 scored / 8 unscorable card refers only to the retained real-hand v16 one-second trial.
Keep uploaded real video, controlled photo motion, randomized simulation, and generated concept illustrations clearly distinct.
Keep synthetic initial conditions hidden from the observer; do not claim arbitrary physics discovery or general 3D reconstruction.
No prediction is available without an actual usable SAM mask. Do not depict manual rectangles as a SAM result.
Owner-private hosted access is not public jury access. The closing public link is the source/evidence repository.
No claimed win probability, prize entitlement, universal accuracy, guaranteed safety, or implemented robot actuation.
